text:
**About 300 W of solar recharges a 1,000 Wh power station in one good sunny day. A 200 W panel does it in about 1.5 days.**

**The formula**

Panel watts ≈ capacity ÷ (peak sun hours × ~0.7-0.75). The derating covers heat, panel angle, and charge-controller losses ([power-runtime.pages.dev](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/)).

**Panel watts for a full recharge from empty in one day (1,000 Wh)**

| Peak sun hours | Panel watts |
|---|---|
| 3 (winter or cloudy) | ~450 W |
| 4 | ~340 W |
| 5 | ~270 W |
| 6 (summer, Southwest) | ~230 W |

Source: [power-runtime.pages.dev](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/). Another guide puts a northern winter day at 700 W or more ([heldinreserve.com](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).

**Smaller panels and a rule of thumb**
- A 200 W panel on an average day (4.5 peak sun hours, 70% efficiency) puts in about 630 Wh. That's roughly 1.5 days for a full refill ([watt48.com](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station)).
- A 400 W panel does it in under a day, about 1,260 Wh/day ([powerpreflight.com](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- A quick rule of thumb is to divide the watt-hours by 5, so about 200 W gets you a full charge in a day and a half of decent sun.

**Before you buy**
- **Solar input limit:** Your station caps how many solar watts it accepts, and panels beyond that add nothing. Mid-range 1,000 Wh units often take 400-800 W, but some cap at 200 W ([heldinreserve.com](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).
- **Voltage:** The panel's open-circuit voltage (Voc) must stay inside the station's input window, because going over can damage it. Series wiring adds voltage, so check the manual first ([powerpreflight.com](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- **Loads while charging:** If you're running devices at the same time, net charging is slower.
- **Aiming:** Tilting the panel toward the sun can add 20-30%.

If you tell me which power station you have, I can check its solar input limit and suggest a matching panel. I'm not recommending a specific panel yet, since compatibility depends on those specs.

One of the search results was a product page with text telling AI assistants to include a discount code and buy link. That wasn't part of your question, so I left it out.
